subject: Service budget & remedy-tier rebalancing for BluePeak
messages:
From: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluepeak.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@bluepeak.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Service budgeting & remedy-tier rebalancing

Connor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we model our expected spend for H2, procurement asked that we reconcile two things in the draft SLA you sent: the uptime floor (we're trying to balance cost vs exposure) and the monthly crediting approach when maintenance or operational incidents occur. Specifically: 

- Can Redwood propose a smoothing approach to monthly credits so we don't see large swings month-to-month?
- We need a clearer maintenance carve-out schedule + example calculations for a 99.9% vs 99.95% uptime comparison.

Attached is our internal availability tolerance spreadsheet (not the final). Happy to jump on a quick call — Priya (cc'd) will handle the finance modeling.

Best,
Alex Chen
Head of Platform, BluePeak Analytics

Attachments: bluepeak_availability_model.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: connor_obrien@redwood.com <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluepeak.com>
Cc: Priya Rao <priya@bluepeak.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service budgeting & remedy-tier rebalancing

Alex —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a short proposal (redwood_sla_proposal_v3.pdf) that tries to address both items with worked examples. TL;DR on our recommendations: 

- Smoothing: introduce a 3-month rolling credit calculation. Months with high credits are averaged so your monthly cashflow impact is bounded; annual aggregation still applies for overall remedy.
- Uptime tiers: keep standard delivered uptime at 99.9% for hosted plans, with an optional 99.95% uplift for a fixed monthly commitment (we show per-token price deltas in the PDF).
- Maintenance carve-out: propose a scheduled maintenance window of up to 6 hours/month, plus a predictable quarterly extended maintenance for major platform upgrades (we include notification and rollback SLAs).

Example included: a 4-hour incident in a month at 99.9% yields X% monthly impact; smoothing spreads that into a reduced effective monthly credit. I included a reference ops_runbook.xlsx that maps incident classes to response and remediation timelines.

If this direction looks close, I'd propose a short working session next week to lock the numbers and produce a redline. Options for next steps: 30-minute call (technical + finance), or we draft a tracked-change SLA for your procurement.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Cell: +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachments: redwood_sla_proposal_v3.pdf (pdf), ops_runbook.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Priya Rao <priya@bluepeak.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluepeak.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 08:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service budgeting & remedy-tier rebalancing

Connor —

Thanks for the proposal. A couple quick questions from our finance lead before we commit to a call: 

1) For the 3-month rolling credit approach, can you share a formulaic example where two consecutive months have incidents (one large, one small)? We want to validate cashflow smoothing assumptions in our procurement model.
2) For the optional 99.95% uplift: what is the minimum commit (monthly spend) to qualify, and how do you calculate the per-token uplift? We saw the delta but need the exact math to plug into our forecast.

Also: how do emergency (unscheduled) maintenance and regional failovers interact with the monthly credit cap? Are failovers to a secondary region counted as an incident for the primary SLA?

If it's easier, we can do a short 30-minute call Wednesday (Apr 6) at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Priya Rao
Procurement Manager, BluePeak Analytics
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.com, Priya Rao <priya@bluepeak.com>, Alex Chen <alex.chen@bluepeak.com>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 4 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Service budgeting & remedy-tier rebalancing

Priya / Alex —

Quick internal note & proposal from Redwood leadership: happy to provision an optional "high-availability uplift" (99.95%) tied to a modest committed monthly spend. Suggested guardrails for the uplift: 

- Commitment threshold: $20k/month in run-rate for the uplift to apply.
- Uplift calculation: a 0.08x per-token multiplier on standard hosted pricing (example math included in the attached PDF).
- Credit smoothing: agree to the 3-month rolling model; additionally cap the monthly remedy to 25% of monthly invoice to avoid outsized single-month credits. Credits above that continue to accrue to annual reconciliation.
- Regional failover: non-disruptive automated regional failover for traffic routing will not be treated as an SLA incident provided we meet documented RTO (regional failover completed within 15 minutes and no traffic loss >1 minute). Anything beyond that would be assessed as an incident for the impacted region.

Monica — please confirm the maintenance carve-out windows and whether the quarterly extended maintenance can be scheduled inside a 30-day agreed calendar.

Next steps for BluePeak: if you accept these guardrails we'll produce a tracked-change SLA for procurement and provide a worked example spreadsheet that shows smoothing math for different incident mixes. Connor — please schedule the Wednesday call if that works.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Platform Sales, Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (650) 555-0133

--
Laura Bennett
Redwood Inference
